issues.display_title: Issue #1128: Floor plan image on the map: overlay with move, resize, rotate and floor placement math
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From PRD #1125, with the answers on #1126. This is the base the other three tasks build on.

Today no floor plan image is drawn on any map. A floor's rooms, walls and markers are stored in the coordinates of its image, so where the image sits on the map is where the floor sits (answer 1a). It is the same position the Map tab's Selected Floor tools edit, level.mapTransform (answer 2).

Scope

  • A floor plan image drawn on a MapLibre map at a given position: center, width in metres, rotation.
  • Handles on the image: drag inside it to move, drag a corner to resize (aspect kept, opposite corner fixed), drag the rotate handle to rotate (Shift snaps to 15°). Dragging the map outside the image still moves the map only.
  • Converting between that position and a floor's saved placement, through the building and project placement above it:
    • read a floor's current image position from its saved placement;
    • write a new image position back as the floor's level.mapTransform.
  • Answer 3a: the size set by the user wins over the scale the scan found.
  • Answer 6: the default position is the project location, 50 m across on the image's longest side.

Acceptance criteria

  • Writing a position and reading it back returns the same position, including on a floor whose building and project are moved, rotated or scaled.
  • After a write, the image's corners land on the floor's own corners on the map.
  • Move, resize and rotate change only the image; map drags outside the image change only the view.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #1129: Wizard Step 3: show, hide and position each floor's image on the map
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From PRD #1125 (R1–R8), with the answers on #1126. Uses the image overlay from #1128.

Scope

  • Step 3 (Order) shows the selected floor's image on the map by default (R1, answer 4). Picking another floor row shows that floor's image instead.
  • The image can be moved, resized and rotated once it is selected (R6–R8).
  • Every floor row that has an image gets an eye icon, always visible, with the tooltip "Show / Hide floor plan" (answer 7). Hiding never removes the upload (R5). The hidden state is not remembered: each time Step 3 opens, the images are shown again (answer 8).
  • Each floor is positioned on its own. A floor that hasn't been positioned yet starts where the floor below it was placed; the lowest one starts at the project location, 50 m across (answers 4 and 6).
  • The position is kept right away, the same way floor names and heights are: leaving the step or reloading the page keeps it (answer 9).
  • When the floors are generated, or the editor is opened without generating, each positioned floor lands where its image was placed, at the size the user set (answers 1a and 3a). A floor nobody positioned is placed as it is today.

Acceptance criteria

  • Uploaded floor plan images appear on the map by default in Step 3, one floor at a time.
  • The eye icon hides and shows the image without removing the upload.
  • The image can be moved, resized and rotated.
  • Positions survive leaving Step 3 and reloading the page.
  • After Generate, each positioned floor sits where its image was placed.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #1130: Editor Add Floor: Continue to a Position Floor Plan map dialog before adding
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From PRD #1125 (R9–R17), with the answers on #1126. Uses the image overlay from #1128.

Scope

  • In Add Floor, once a floor plan image is uploaded, Add Floor Only and Add & Scan Floor are replaced by Continue (R9). Without an image, the dialog works as it does today (R9, assumption 3).
  • Continue opens a large map dialog titled Position Floor Plan, laid out like the panorama import map dialog (R10, answer 5).
  • The dialog opens framed on the project's existing floors, with the new image placed over them (answer 10). The existing floors are shown for reference.
  • The image can be moved, resized and rotated, and the map can be moved (R11–R15).
  • Add & Scan Floor is the primary action and Add Floor Only the secondary one (UX table), with a short line saying what each does (Risk 4).
    • Add Floor Only adds the floor with the image position, and no scan runs (R16).
    • Add & Scan Floor adds the floor with the image position and scans it. The scanned rooms land on the image (R17).
  • A failed scan keeps the floor at its position, and Retry Scan works as it does today.

Acceptance criteria

  • Add Floor shows Continue after an image is uploaded.
  • Continue opens the large map dialog with the image.
  • The image can be moved, resized and rotated, and the map can be moved.
  • Add Floor Only adds the floor at the image position without scanning.
  • Add & Scan Floor adds the floor at the image position and scans it.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #1131: Editor Edit Floor: map marker opens Edit Floor Plan Position dialog
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From PRD #1125 (R18–R27), with the answers on #1126. Uses the image overlay from #1128.

Scope

  • In the editor's Edit Floor list, floors with a floor plan image show a map marker icon (R18). Floors without one don't. The icon is not shown in Step 3's Edit Floor (assumption 1).
  • The icon opens a large map dialog titled Edit Floor Plan Position, centered on the image at the floor's current position (R19–R20, answer 11).
  • The image can be moved, resized and rotated, and the map can be moved (R21–R24). The building's other floors are shown for reference.
  • Cancel closes without changing anything (R25).
  • Save stores the position and moves the floor's rooms, markers and panoramas with it (R26, answer 1a). Save is independent of the other Edit Floor fields (answer 12). A message confirms the save.
  • Save is one step in the editor's undo history (answer 16).
  • The floor's name, height, order and contents stay the same (R27). Moving the building later moves its floors and their images with it (answer 15).

Acceptance criteria

  • Only floors with an image show the map marker icon, and only in the editor.
  • The dialog opens on the floor's current position.
  • Cancel leaves the position unchanged. Reopening shows the old position.
  • Save moves the floor to the new position. Reopening shows the new position.
  • Ctrl+Z after Save restores the previous position.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.
